definitions.explanation: Something that strongly calls to mind or vividly evokes an image of something else. Almost always used in the pattern 〜を{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせる (to be reminiscent of) or 〜を{彷彿|ほうふつ}させる.

examples.japanese: {昭和|しょうわ}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}を{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせる{街並|まちな}み。
examples.english: A streetscape reminiscent of the Showa era.

examples.japanese: その{演技|えんぎ}は{若|わか}き{日|ひ}の{父|ちち}を{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせた。
examples.english: That performance was reminiscent of his father in his younger days.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}ローマを{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせる{壮大|そうだい}な{建築|けんちく}が{観光客|かんこうきゃく}を{魅了|みりょう}している。
examples.english: The grand architecture, reminiscent of ancient Rome, captivates tourists.

notes:
{彷彿|ほうふつ} means to vividly evoke or call to mind something else. It is almost never used as a standalone word — it appears in fixed patterns.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜を{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせる: to be reminiscent of ~, to evoke ~ (most common)
- 〜を{彷彿|ほうふつ}させる: slightly less formal variant of the above

EXAMPLES OF USE:
- {昭和|しょうわ}を{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせる: reminiscent of the Showa era
- {若|わか}き{日|ひ}を{彷彿|ほうふつ}とさせる: evocative of one's younger days

REGISTER:
A literary, written expression. Common in reviews, essays, and descriptive journalism. Not typically used in casual speech — {思|おも}い{出|だ}させる (to remind of) or 〜みたいだ (like ~) are more natural alternatives in conversation.

WRITING:
The kanji {彷彿|ほうふつ} are rarely used outside this word. Sometimes written in hiragana as ほうふつ.
